core_meaning.short_meaning: Persian name of the eighth Iranian month, “the Waters”; not the Arabic name Abān
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aaban (آبان, Ābān) is a Persian name for the eighth month of the Iranian solar calendar, roughly late October to late November. It comes from Persian āb, “water”: in Zoroastrian tradition the month, and the tenth day of every month, are dedicated to the Waters, and Persian dictionaries also list Ābān as the name of the angel in charge of water. Because Latin spellings overlap, Aaban is often confused with the Arabic name Abān (أبان, also written Aban), a separate name meaning “clear, evident” that was borne by the Companion Abān ibn Saʿīd.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Ābān, “the waters”; the eighth month of the Iranian solar calendar
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Dehkhoda’s Persian dictionary lists آبان as the eighth month of the solar year, as the tenth day of the traditional month, and as the name of the angel in charge of water. The Persian names dictionary Farhang-e Nāmhā gives the Pahlavi sense as “waters”. Encyclopaedia Iranica describes Ābān Māh as the eighth month of the Zoroastrian year, dedicated to the Waters, with the feast Ābānagān on its tenth day. The separate Arabic name Abān (أبان) is explained in Arabic name references as a past-tense form of the verb abāna, meaning clear or evident.

etymology.morphology: Persian word formed on āb, “water”; Pahlavi sense “the waters”. Used as a month name, a day name and the name of the angel of water.
etymology.etymological_meaning: The Waters; the month and day dedicated to them in the Zoroastrian calendar.
etymology.etymology_explanation: Persian ābān is recorded in Farhang-e Nāmhā as Pahlavi for “waters” and in Dehkhoda as a month, day and angel name. Encyclopaedia Iranica places the month in the Zoroastrian calendar, dedicated to the Waters. The Arabic name Abān (أبان) has an unrelated origin: it is generally derived from Arabic abāna, “to be clear” (root b-y-n), although sources do not all agree on the derivation of this specific name.
etymology.false_etymology_warning: Do not treat Persian Ābān (آبان) and Arabic Abān (أبان) as one word because their Latin spellings overlap, and do not infer a Qur’anic status, personality trait or popularity from either spelling.

language_notes.primary: Persian is the language of the recorded form آبان.
language_notes.usage: Other scripts are transliterations of the name into those writing systems, not independent origins. The Arabic name أبان is a separate word.

origin.origin_explanation: The documented form آبان is Persian and names the eighth month of the Iranian solar calendar, a month dedicated to the Waters in Zoroastrian tradition. The Arabic name أبان is a different name with a different origin.

religion.primary_association: Persian cultural name used in Muslim communities
religion.religious_status: Culturally used; not inherently a doctrinal term
religion.religious_explanation: The word is a Persian calendar and water name with Zoroastrian background. Muslim families may use it as a given name, but this record cites no Qur’anic verse, hadith or Islamic ruling that establishes it as a specifically Islamic or prescribed name. The similar Arabic name Abān is separate and is attested among the Companions.

quranic_status.note: Aaban is not identified as a Qur’anic personal name, so no Qur’anic basis is claimed.

hadith_status.note: The Companion Abān ibn Saʿīd appears in hadith narrations, for example the Khaybar account in Sahih al-Bukhari 4238. This concerns the person, not a ruling on the name, and applies to Arabic Abān rather than Persian Ābān.

prophetic_status.note: No verified source establishes Aaban or Abān as the name of a prophet.

companion_status.note: Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ al-Umawī al-Qurashī (أبان بن سعيد), a Companion and scribe appointed by the Prophet ﷺ over Bahrain. His name is the Arabic Abān, so this does not by itself show Companion usage of the Persian name Ābān.

islamic_naming_context.context: Muslim communities, including the Persianate world and South Asia
islamic_naming_context.interpretation: The documented meaning of Persian Ābān is a calendar month and “the Waters”, not a personal virtue. If a family means the Arabic name Abān (أبان), the meaning is “clear, evident” and the name has Companion-era bearers. Any further symbolism is personal interpretation.
islamic_naming_context.important_distinction: Muslim use of the name is not evidence that the Persian word is Qur’anic or religiously prescribed.

cultural_context.cultural_meaning: In Persian and Zoroastrian tradition the month of Ābān and its tenth day are dedicated to the Waters. The tenth day was celebrated as the feast Ābānagān, when people went to streams, lakes or the sea to pray and make offerings. Classical Persian poets also use the month name.
cultural_context.personal_name_interpretation: Families may choose the name for its Persian, water-related and calendar associations. This is personal interpretation rather than an independently established meaning of the given name.
cultural_context.interpretation_warning: Keep the calendar-month definition, the Zoroastrian background, the Arabic name Abān and modern personal-name usage distinct.

spiritual_meaning.meaning: No separate spiritual meaning is asserted for the given name beyond the documented Zoroastrian dedication of the month to the Waters.

personality_associations.note: No verified basis links this name to specific personality traits.

numerology.meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaban total 10 (1+1+2+1+5), which reduces to 1, associated with leadership, independence and initiative. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

urdu.name: آبان
urdu.meaning: ایرانی شمسی تقویم کا آٹھواں مہینہ؛ ‘پانیوں’ سے منسوب فارسی نام
urdu.long_meaning: آبان فارسی نام ہے جو ایرانی شمسی تقویم کے آٹھویں مہینے کا نام ہے (تقریباً اکتوبر کے آخر سے نومبر کے آخر تک)۔ یہ لفظ فارسی ‘آب’ (پانی) سے ماخوذ ہے؛ زرتشتی روایت میں یہ مہینہ اور ہر مہینے کا دسواں دن پانیوں کے لیے مخصوص ہے، اور فارسی لغات میں آبان پانی پر مامور فرشتے کا نام بھی درج ہے۔ آبان کو عربی نام اَبان (أبان) سے الگ سمجھنا چاہیے، جس کا مفہوم ‘واضح، ظاہر’ ہے اور جو صحابیِ رسول ابان بن سعید رضی اللہ عنہ کا نام تھا۔

persian.name: آبان
persian.long_meaning: آبان نام ماه هشتم تقویم خورشیدی ایران است. این واژه از «آب» می‌آید؛ در سنت زرتشتی این ماه و روز دهم هر ماه به آب‌ها اختصاص دارد و در فرهنگ‌های فارسی آبان نام فرشتهٔ موکل بر آب نیز ثبت شده است. آبان را باید از نام عربی «اَبان» (أبان) به معنای «روشن و آشکار» که نام صحابی پیامبر، ابان بن سعید، بود جدا دانست.

hindi.name: आबान
hindi.meaning: ईरानी सौर कैलेंडर का आठवाँ महीना; ‘जल’ से जुड़ा फ़ारसी नाम
hindi.long_meaning: आबान फ़ारसी नाम है, जो ईरानी सौर कैलेंडर के आठवें महीने का नाम है। यह शब्द फ़ारसी ‘आब’ (पानी) से जुड़ा है; ज़रथुस्त्री परंपरा में यह महीना और हर महीने का दसवाँ दिन जल को समर्पित है, और फ़ारसी शब्दकोशों में आबान जल पर नियुक्त फ़रिश्ते का नाम भी दर्ज है। इसे अरबी नाम अबान (أبان) से अलग समझना चाहिए, जिसका अर्थ ‘स्पष्ट, प्रकट’ है और जो सहाबी अबान इब्न सईद का नाम था।

pashto.meaning: د ایران د لمریز کلیز اتمه میاشت؛ د اوبو نوم
pashto.long_meaning: آبان د فارسي ژبې نوم دی او د ایران د لمریز هجري کلیز اتمه میاشت ښيي. دا نوم د فارسي «آب» (اوبه) سره تړاو لري؛ د زرتشتي دود له مخې دا میاشت او د هرې میاشتې لسمه ورځ اوبو ته ځانګړې ده. له عربي نوم «ابان» (أبان) سره باید ګډوډ نشي، چې معنا یې «څرګند، روښانه» ده او د رسول الله ﷺ د یو صحابي، ابان بن سعید، نوم و.

arabic.name: آبان
arabic.meaning: آبان: اسم فارسي للشهر الثامن في التقويم الشمسي الإيراني، ومعناه «المياه»؛ وهو غير اسم «أبان» العربي.
arabic.long_meaning: آبان اسم فارسي للشهر الثامن من التقويم الشمسي الإيراني. وهو مأخوذ من الفارسية «آب» أي الماء؛ ففي التقليد الزرادشتي يُخصَّص هذا الشهر واليوم العاشر من كل شهر للمياه، وتذكر المعاجم الفارسية «آبان» اسمًا للملَك الموكَّل بالماء. ويختلف عن الاسم العربي «أبان» (من الفعل أبانَ بمعنى ظهر واتضح)، ومن حمله الصحابي أبان بن سعيد بن العاص رضي الله عنه.

faq.a: Aaban (آبان, Ābān) is the Persian name of the eighth month of the Iranian solar calendar. It comes from Persian āb, “water”, and in Zoroastrian tradition the month is dedicated to the Waters.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aaban?
faq.a: Persian. Ābān is a Middle Persian (Pahlavi) word for “the waters” and the name of the eighth month. The tenth day of the month was traditionally celebrated as a festival, Ābānagān.

Not in the form آبان. Aaban normally transliterates the Persian name Ābān. A separate Arabic name, Abān (أبان), also exists and is often spelled Aban in English; it is generally explained as coming from the Arabic verb abāna, “to be or become clear”.

faq.q: Is Aaban the same as Aban?
faq.a: The spellings overlap, but the names can be different. Persian آبان (Ābān) is the month and water name, while Arabic أبان (Abān) means “clear, evident”. Check the Persian or Arabic script to see which one a family means.

Aaban is a Persian cultural name that Muslim families may use, but it is not a Qur’anic term or a name prescribed by Islam. The similar Arabic name Abān has an Islamic history: it was borne by the Companion Abān ibn Saʿīd.
This record does not identify Aaban or Abān as a name that appears in the Qur’an, and no Qur’anic basis is claimed.

faq.q: Was there a Companion named Aban?
faq.a: Yes. Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ (أبان بن سعيد) was a Companion of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and one of his scribes, and was appointed over Bahrain. His name is the Arabic Abān, not the Persian month name Ābān.

faq.q: What does Aaban mean in Urdu?
faq.a: اس ریکارڈ میں آبان کا بنیادی مفہوم ایرانی شمسی تقویم کا آٹھواں مہینہ ہے، جو فارسی ‘آب’ (پانی) سے ماخوذ ہے۔ یہ عربی نام اَبان (أبان) سے الگ ہے، جس کا مطلب ‘واضح، ظاہر’ ہے۔
In Persian it is pronounced roughly “aa-BAAN”, with a long first and last vowel and stress on the last syllable. The Arabic name Abān is pronounced “a-BAAN” with a short first vowel.

faq.q: Is Aaban a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The Arabic name Abān is masculine and its documented historical bearers were men. Persian dictionaries list Ābān as a month and water-angel name without specifying a gender. Aaban is therefore most often treated as a boy's name, but no modern usage statistics are published here.
